svg.title: Mockup 03: an incident, mute and history
svg.text: 03 · An incident: its timeline, what to check, mute, and the day's history (event crew)
One page per incident: what happened when, who was told and who is on it, the fixes tried, and the next step in words.
Use case: a crew member opens an alert from Discord or Health, acks it, mutes a screen that is being replaced, and looks back at the day
A · The incident page at 1280 px, acked, the fix not possible while the screen is offline
Identify and Reload need the screen online
Its last heartbeat; its zone Main hall played the run of show.
Incident opened. Screen 1 in the same zone still shows it.
One message; it changes in place as this does.
A reload needs the screen online; nothing to try remotely.
Acked by Player Two in Discord
Reminders stop. The message says who is on it.
"Going to the PC, power strip looks off."
Add a note for the crew…
Is the screen's PC on, with the browser on
Is the network up at the screen? Screen 1
in the same hall is online, so the hall's
Once the PC is back the screen comes
back by itself: its cookie keeps it paired.
Moments, food and the run of show go on.
The screen's sound plays from screen 1.
B · The incident on a phone

svg.text: C · Mute: one subject, for a set time

g.text: No alerts, reminders or fixes for it until then.
Kept for the event's life; who acted shows as long

svg.text: The page's crew actions as one band above its parts (amendment 3). Actions that cannot work now say why instead of failing: Identify and Reload are typed
screen commands (built), delivered only to an online screen (D11).
The timeline is the incident's whole story, kept for the event's life (D8). It writes "no automatic fix" and "blocked" as entries, never as fake state changes
Words per alert kind: what to check and what still works, filled with the facts (L2). The raw check is the grey last line, for whoever needs it.
